title: pager-root-cause-sketch-harold-2026-05-02
content:
TL;DR: short spike in 95/99 latency for hosted-api text-generation routes around 2026-05-02T03:10Z. Symptoms point to KV-cache miss storms + batching slowdown after a rolling deploy of an optimized attention kernel. No data exfiltration, no customer data loss. Pager triggered due to sustained p99 > 1.5s for 3m.

Timeline (rough):
- 03:07Z: first alerts from synthetic probing (eu-west) p95/p99 rising
- 03:09Z: customer page (high volume) + internal prometheus alerts on serving-runtime queue-length
- 03:10Z: rolling deploy (canary -> primary) of attention-kernel v1.2.3 started by release-engineering (auto)
- 03:12Z: spike in number of cold KV cache misses and increased tail latency on model xglm-70b-inf
- 03:19Z: we throttled canary and reverted kernel on 2 nodes; tail latency dropped gradually
- 03:27Z: full revert completed, p99 back to baseline by 03:33Z

Initial hypothesis: the new kernel introduced a regressed prefetch pattern that caused more frequent KV cache invalidations under our serving runtime's continuous-batching heuristics. Cache miss storms + longer per-token CPU time increased queuing, which in turn increased observed p99.

What I checked quickly:
- Prometheus: per-node token-processing-time increased ~2.3x on impacted nodes (node ids: gpu-ded-12, gpu-ded-13)
- KV cache hit-rate dropped from 98% -> 78% for model xglm-70b-inf during spike
- Batching stats: average batch size shrank as backpressure prevented bundling; queue length rose to > 400 requests on affected pods
- Pod logs: OOMs? none. GC spikes? small JVM-ish pause spikes on control-plane metrics but not correlated
- GPU metrics: util stayed ~70-85% but GPU SM time per token rose slightly. CPU sys time on runtime host increased (kernel syscalls for cache mgmt?)

Immediate runbook TODOs (for my follow-up and handoff):
- [ ] Attach timeline + graphs to JIRA-INC-4821 (owner: Harold)
- [ ] Get exact kernel change diff from PR #987 and ask release-eng for profiling notes (owner: Harold)
- [ ] Add a short test in CI that runs synthetic prefix distributions against attention-kernel v1.2.x to catch KV/cache regressions (owner: Samir)
- [ ] Add a temporary alert: if kv_cache_hit_rate drops > 10% vs 1h baseline -> page SRE (owner: eng-sre)
- [ ] Draft a short blameless postmortem skeleton (owner: Maya)

Commands / quick repro steps I ran: (paste into prod debug session carefully)
- kubectl -n serving get pods -l app=serving-runtime -o wide
- kubectl logs -f pod/gpu-ded-12 -c runtime --since=20m | grep "kv_cache" | tail -n 200
- curl -sS http://metrics.internal/prometheus/api/v1/query?query=kv_cache_hit_ratio{model=\"xglm-70b-inf\"}
- python tools/synthetic_probe.py --model xglm-70b-inf --prefix-dist small,medium --qps 200 --duration 300 --backend=staging-sim

Notes-to-self for deeper analysis:
- Need to correlate batch-formation latency histogram with cache miss events. I suspect there is a feedback loop: more cache misses -> smaller batches -> higher per-token overhead -> more misses.
- Check the kernel's code path for KV prefetch; does it reorder reads such that our cache TTL logic is invalidated?
- Re-run with kernel + explicit cache-warm step in dev env to see whether warm path behaves differently.

Customer-facing impact:
- Small number of high-volume customers experienced visible slow responses for ~15 minutes. No dropped or corrupted responses observed. Recommend proactive note from CS for affected customers if we get an inbound from larger accounts.

Handover notes for next on-call:
- If you see a similar latency pattern, first check kv_cache_hit_ratio and batch size. If hit_ratio < 85% AND avg_batch_size < 8 -> escalate to runtime-eng and consider immediate revert of recent kernel deploys.
- Look for accompanying queue-length > 300 on any serving pod.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Does the kernel have a microbenchmark that simulates our prefix/multistream workload? If not, add one.
- Is there an observable change in the kernel that affects memory access patterns (NUMA binding, prefetch instructions)?
- Should we add a fast compare job that replays a sample of production prefixes against canary kernel before traffic shift? (quick mitigation suggestion)

Misc scratch (things I scribbled in Slack):
- "revert if kv hit < 90% in canary for > 3m" - might be too aggressive, but useful as a temp gate
- asked RE to share perf flamegraphs for kernel PR (waiting)

Reference links (internal):
- Incident ticket: JIRA-INC-4821
- Kernel PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/987
- Quick graphs: https://metrics.internal/d/abc/kv-cache-incident-graphs?from=2026-05-02T03:00Z&to=2026-05-02T03:40Z

End notes:
- This doc is a quick scratchpad; will flesh into a proper postmortem if JIRA needs it. Leaving TODOs simple so next rotation can pick up.

Harold C.
2026-05-03 09:12 PDT
